related_questions.question: How to get immunization records in NY?

text_blocks.snippet: To obtain immunization records in New York, start by checking the New York State Immunization Information System (NYSIIS) or the Citywide Immunization Registry (CIR) if you are in New York City. If your records aren't in these systems, contact your healthcare provider, or the school your child attended. You can also request records online or by mail/fax through the CIR website.
snippet_highlighted_words: checking the New York State Immunization Information System (NYSIIS) or the Citywide Immunization Registry (CIR) if you are in New York City

list.snippet: NYSIIS is a state-wide electronic registry that holds immunization records for New Yorkers.
The Citywide Immunization Registry (CIR) is specific to New York City.
You can access the CIR through My Vaccine Record.
If the records are not found in NYSIIS or CIR, contact the healthcare provider who administered the vaccinations, or your current provider.
Schools in New York maintain immunization records for students, typically keeping them for a few years after the student leaves or graduates.
NYC.gov offers a way to request records online using options like IDNYC, DMV, or other personal identifiers.
Complete the Immunization Record Request Application (available online or by mail).
Include a copy of your photo ID.
Mail or fax the completed form.
The Immunization Action Coalition (IAC) has helpful resources.
Consider keeping a digital copy of your immunization records for future reference.
If you cannot locate records, consider getting repeat vaccinations, after consulting with a healthcare provider.
